headline: Meta's Muse AI creates custom 'spaces' for personalized app experiences
summary: The new "spaces" feature allows users to build app-like experiences such as shopping hubs or school dashboards directly within the Muse AI assistant, updating information in the background.
details: Meta is rolling out a new feature called "spaces" for its Muse AI assistant, enabling users to create customized, app-like experiences directly within the app. These spaces can function as shopping hubs, school dashboards, music trackers, or even trivia games.

Users can interact with these custom spaces by checking off items, adding notes, and making edits. Muse can also connect to relevant apps to automatically update pricing, dates, and other information in the background.

Creating a new space involves describing the desired functionality to Muse, which can then be further tweaked through conversational prompts. This allows for a highly personalized and dynamic user experience.

Spaces can be added to the Muse app's sidebar, moved to the main tab, and scheduled to appear at specific times. For example, a weekly planner can be prioritized during weekdays and swapped for weekend plans on Saturdays.

The "spaces" feature is being deployed to all Muse users, alongside a "specialized" version of Meta's Muse Wonder AI model. Meta is also exploring future capabilities, including ways for users to share and collaborate on their custom spaces.

headline: Ten major companies launch agentic commerce products including OpenAI, Google, and Amazon
summary: OpenAI, Google, Amazon, PayPal, Shopify, Visa, and Mastercard are among the giants rolling out AI agents that find, choose, or pay for items on users' behalf.
details: Agentic commerce involves AI agents finding, choosing, or paying for items on a person's behalf. Real-world examples include ChatGPT Instant Checkout, Google agentic checkout, and Amazon Buy for Me, each with confirmed launch dates and public sources.

OpenAI launched Instant Checkout on September 29, 2025, allowing US ChatGPT users to buy from US Etsy sellers directly within the chat, with Stripe processing payments. In November 2025, OpenAI also added shopping research capabilities, enabling personalized buyer's guides.

Google began rolling out agentic checkout on Search in November 2025, including an AI Mode for eligible US merchants like Wayfair. This update also introduced 'Let Google Call,' where AI contacts local stores to inquire about stock and prices.

Amazon is testing 'Buy for Me,' which allows the app to purchase items from a brand's own website on the customer's behalf if Amazon doesn't sell it. Additionally, Rufus, Amazon's shopping assistant, helps all US customers with product questions, comparisons, and order tracking.

PayPal and Perplexity launched Instant Buy on November 25, 2025, enabling US users to check out directly within Perplexity from various merchants. On January 8, 2026, PayPal announced it would power Copilot Checkout, allowing seamless shopping within Copilot.

On December 10, 2025, Shopify introduced Agentic Storefronts, simplifying the process for merchants to send their products to AI platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot. Orders are then attributed back to the respective AI channel.

The card networks also made early moves into agentic commerce. Mastercard launched Agent Pay on April 29, 2025, featuring Agentic Tokens and requiring registered agents. Visa followed the next day with Intelligent Commerce, offering tokenized credentials and consumer-set spending limits for agents.

Several open standards underpin these developments, including the Agentic Commerce Protocol from OpenAI and Stripe for agent-merchant checkout. Google's AP2, announced with over 60 organizations, records user authorizations, while its Universal Commerce Protocol was developed with major retailers and endorsed by payment partners.

Key players in this ecosystem include AI platforms like OpenAI, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Perplexity, where shopping occurs. Commerce platforms such as Shopify and Etsy connect merchants, while payment companies like Stripe, PayPal, Visa, Mastercard, and American Express handle transactions and build trust.

Startups are focusing on the underlying infrastructure rather than storefronts. A notable example is Cymbio, a multi-channel orchestration platform acquired by PayPal in February 2026, which helps brands integrate with agentic surfaces like Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity.
AI agents are now actively shopping for you. Major tech and payment companies have launched products where AI finds, chooses, or pays for goods on your behalf.
